videos.title: The System part of the menu
videos.intro: The System part of the menu holds the screens that belong to no single department. In this video you will see each one, and who uses it.

scenes.say: System is the last section of the menu. This is how the owner sees it.
Approvals is everything waiting on you, from every part of the system. You approve or refuse it right there.
Notifications is the bell's list, on a page of its own.
System health shows what the server is doing, from its own records. Only the owner and administrators see it.
Design system is a tool for the people who build the system. It is only on the test computer.
Room systems is marked Not built yet. Door locks, room phones and minibars will live here.
Settings is the third space, in the switcher at the top.
Your own menu may be shorter. Every screen you may open is still one search away. Click Find a screen, or press Control K, and type the first letters of its name.
Here the Inventory Manager finds Approvals. It says Not in your menu, but it is still theirs to open.

videos.outro: Users and Integrations are not in the menu either. Those allowed to open them find them the same way.

videos.title: Who approves what
videos.intro: Some things wait for a second person's yes before they count. In this video you will see what they are, and who says yes.

scenes.say: Every request goes to the same Approvals screen. Somebody asks, with a reason, and somebody else decides.
A purchase request is raised on Purchasing. The general manager approves every purchase, whatever the amount.
A cash expense is money paid out of a drawer: the front desk's, or a restaurant's tin. The general manager or the owner decides it. Never an administrator.
Equipment leaving the store waits for the Inventory Manager. When they are away, the owner, an administrator or the general manager decides instead. Retiring a tagged item can wait for them too.
Nobody approves their own request. The general manager asked for this cash expense, so it waits for the owner.
A decision stays. An approved or refused request cannot be decided again. To go ahead after a refusal, raise a new request.

videos.outro: The group owner may decide any request. Next, the general manager decides two of them.

videos.title: Approving or refusing
videos.intro: In this video the general manager decides two purchase requests from the Inventory Manager. One is refused, and one is approved.

scenes.say: Open Approvals, in the System part of the menu.
Waiting lists every request that still needs a decision, newest first.
Each card says what kind of request it is. In orange, it opens the whole request on its own screen.
Under it, what it is for, in the words of the person who asked.
Then the amount, who asked, and when.
To refuse, a note is required. To approve, it is not.
Here the manager types why the gas cylinders are refused: four are on deposit already.
Then taps Refuse. The message says it is refused, and they have been told why.
To approve, tap Approve. The tea cups were approved this way, and can now be ordered from a supplier.

videos.outro: Refuse with no note is not accepted. Neither button can be undone, so read the card first.

videos.title: Not yours to decide, and what was decided
videos.intro: In this video you will see a request you may not decide, and where to find what was decided, and by whom.

scenes.say: Approvals lists every request waiting at the hotel. This one is a cash expense: milk for the kitchen, from the restaurant's tin.
There are no buttons. The general manager asked for it, so the sentence says they cannot be the one who approves it. It waits for the owner.
To see the decided requests too, tap Everything at the top right. Those still waiting come first.
The gas cylinders are marked Refused.
Under them, who refused them, and the note they wrote.
The tea cups are marked Approved, by the general manager.
Equipment requests show here too. This one, the air conditioner for room 205, was approved by the Inventory Manager.

videos.outro: The person who decides sees who asked, and the person who asked sees who decided.

videos.title: When you asked: reading the answer
videos.intro: You asked for something. In this video you will see where to read the answer.

scenes.say: The Inventory Manager opens Purchasing, and clicks the request for the gas cylinders.
The request keeps it all: what it was for, the store it goes to, the total, who asked, when, and who decided.
Refused shows beside the request's number.
Under it, who refused it, and their note.
A decision stays on the record. To go ahead after this, raise a new request.
The Inventory Manager decides equipment requests, but Approvals is not in their shorter menu. Click Find a screen, and type the first letters of Approvals.
Approvals is found. It says Not in your menu, and it is still theirs to open. Press Enter.

videos.outro: A request still waiting says Waiting for the general manager. A cash expense shows its answer on its drawer's line.

videos.title: Cash expenses
videos.intro: Money paid out of a drawer, for milk, a taxi or a repair, is a cash expense. Every one waits for a yes.

scenes.say: To record one, open Cashiering at the front desk, or Close restaurant day in a restaurant. Under In and out of the drawer, tap Record. Choose Paid out, or Expense, type how much and what it was for, and tap Record.
It arrives in Approvals as a cash expense, named by its drawer and your own words.
The general manager or the owner decides it. Never the person who paid it out.
While it waits, the drawer's line says Waiting for a yes, not taken off the drawer yet. The drawer is still expected to hold that money.
Approved, it is taken off what the drawer should hold, even if the drawer has closed since.
Refused, the line says Not approved, with the note. The money is a shortage on that drawer, and nothing more.
A waiting expense does not stop the close. The part of a shortage it explains needs no reason. Only the rest does.

videos.outro: Record an expense as soon as the money leaves the drawer, in plain words. It is the line somebody asks about tomorrow.

videos.title: The bell and Notifications
videos.intro: The bell tells you what needs attention. In this video you will read it, and its page, Notifications.

scenes.say: Click the bell at the top. The list opens on the right, with how many you have not read.
Each notice says what needs attention, and where. Here, an arrival not yet checked in. Click it to open its screen.
A notice goes by itself when the thing is done. Check the guest in, and it is gone.
Mark all as read clears the count in this window, until the page is reloaded.
Notifications, in the System part of the menu, is the same list on a page. Open, on the right of each notice, goes to the screen it is about.
You see what your role may see. The Inventory Manager reads that a balance is outstanding, without the amount or the guest's name. Here, a crockery count is due.
Its kind is approval: something for a manager to look at. It is not a request in Approvals.

videos.outro: Remember: requests waiting on you are not on the bell. Open Approvals to see them.

videos.title: Approvals in short
videos.intro: Here are approvals, cash expenses and notifications, in short.
checklist: You need something bought: Purchasing, Ask to buy, say what it is for, Send for approval.
You pay cash out of a drawer: record it. Paid out at the desk, Expense in a restaurant.
Something waits on you: Approvals, Waiting. Approve, or type a note and Refuse.
You asked for it: you cannot decide it. Read the answer on the request, or on the drawer's line.
Refused, and still needed: raise a new request. The first decision stays.
The bell shows a number: click it, click a notice, and do the work. The notice goes by itself.
videos.outro: That is approvals, cash expenses and notifications. Thank you for watching.
